languages._comment_docker_repo: Uses the single official docker.io/library/ruby image throughout (no repo-path migration the way .NET/Java needed) -- confirmed live via the Docker Hub Registry API's tag-list endpoint across the whole tracked range (1.9.3 through 4.0.6). The '-slim' tag suffix is used throughout, matching this project's other Debian-based language images. Real, live-verified Debian codename history per minor (via 'docker run ruby:X.Y-slim cat /etc/os-release', not guessed/estimated -- an earlier pass had guessed 2.1 was still wheezy based on the '-slim-<codename>' suffixed-tag history alone, which was WRONG: its bare tag was actually already rebuilt onto jessie, confirmed live, and pointing its apt sources at wheezy instead caused an unresolvable package conflict against the jessie libc6/apt/dpkg already baked in): jessie (2.1, 2.2), stretch (2.3), buster (2.4, 2.5), bullseye (2.6, 2.7, 3.0), bookworm (3.1 -- no trixie rebuild exists for 3.1 either, since Ruby 3.1 reached its own EOL 2025-03-31 before trixie became the default base), trixie (3.2, 3.3, 3.4, 4.0, the current default for every still-patched minor). The bare 'X.Y-slim' floating tag for a minor that has stopped receiving new Ruby patches stays frozen at whatever codename it was last built under -- it is NOT automatically rebuilt onto newer Debian bases the way an actively-patched minor's tag is. jessie/stretch/buster are all long past deb.debian.org/security.debian.org cutoff (confirmed via the same class of live 404 this project already hit for Go/Node/PHP's own EOL-era images) and need the SAME archive.debian.org sources.list redirect + '-o Acquire::Check-Valid-Until=false' + '--allow-unauthenticated' fix already established in lang_go.py/lang_node.py/lang_php.py -- this affects every minor whose bare tag currently resolves to jessie/stretch/buster, i.e. 2.1, 2.2, 2.3, 2.4, and 2.5 (five of the fifteen tracked minors; 1.9/2.0 are excluded outright as schema-1/unpullable). 2.6 and newer currently resolve to bullseye or later, not yet needing this fix as of this writing.
languages._comment_35_renamed_to_40: '3.5' never shipped as a real, numbered stable Ruby release -- confirmed live via both the Docker Hub tags API (only '3.5.0-preview1'/'3.5-rc' pre-release tags exist, pushed 2025-11-19; no bare '3.5.0' or '3.5-slim' GA tag was ever published) and ruby-lang.org's own official release announcement: the version developed under the '3.5' working name during 2025 was renamed to Ruby 4.0.0 before General Availability, released 2025-12-25 as the traditional Christmas release marking Ruby's 30th anniversary (www.ruby-lang.org/en/news/2025/12/25/ruby-4-0-0-released/). Listed below with include:false and a null release_date purely as an explicit 'this number was working-name-only, never a real GA release' reference row, matching this registry's convention (already used elsewhere in this project, e.g. PHP's '6.0') of documenting numbering gaps rather than silently omitting them.
languages._comment_19_20_schema1: '1.9' and '2.0''s bare '-slim' tags are still schema-1 (Docker Image Manifest v2, Schema 1) on Docker Hub -- confirmed live via 'docker manifest inspect ruby:1.9-slim'/'ruby:2.0-slim', both returning 'unsupported manifest media type ... application/vnd.docker.distribution.manifest.v1+prettyjws'. Modern Docker refuses to pull schema-1 images outright ('support Docker Image manifest version 2, schema 1 has been removed'), the exact same class of gap already documented for golang:1.2-1.4 in the Go registry. '2.1' (also wheezy-based) is schema-2 and pulls fine -- confirmed live -- so this is NOT a blanket wheezy-era problem, just these two specific tags. Listed below with include:false, keeping their real release dates, matching this registry's own reference-row convention; '2.1' is the earliest real, buildable Ruby minor.

frameworks.name: Rails
frameworks.notes: Version history and every Ruby-floor value pulled directly from RubyGems.org's own /api/v1/versions/rails.json (519 published version entries; live-verified 2026-08). Majors 0-2 are kept as compatibility:[] REFERENCE-ONLY rows: RubyGems.org's own created_at timestamp for every 0.x/1.x entry (and most of 2.x) is an identical '2009-07-25' bulk-migration artifact (RubyGems.org itself launched in 2009 and backfilled pre-existing gems with its own launch date, not the gem's real release date) -- confirmed NOT real history by cross-checking against Rails' own release history: the real first Rails release was 0.5 (2004-07-24), Rails 1.0 shipped 2005-12-14, and Rails 2.0 shipped 2007-12-07. All three majors also predate Rails' own adoption of Bundler/Gemfile-based dependency management (introduced at 3.0, 2010-08-29) -- structurally the same 'no dependency-manager era' reasoning this project already uses for PHP's Laravel 1/2/3 (pre-Composer). Every floor value for majors 3-8 is each major's LATEST patch's declared required_ruby_version (this registry's standard convention, matching PHP's), confirmed live via RubyGems, not the framework's own release-announcement page. Rails 5+ also ships a real, lighter '--api'-only mode ('rails new --api', a genuine reduced middleware/routing stack skipping views/assets/sessions) -- a real touch-code-level difference worth noting for whoever writes lang_ruby.py, but not a separate registry bucket since it is a boot flag on the same gem version, not a different dependency.

frameworks.name: Sinatra
frameworks.notes: Every date/floor pulled live from RubyGems.org's versions API (108 published entries). Major 0's RubyGems-recorded date (2009-07-25) is the same bulk-migration artifact documented on Rails' major 0/1/2 above -- Sinatra's real first release was 2007-09-09 (Blake Mizerany's original release), kept here as the documented real date but not load-bearing since major 0 declares no required_ruby_version at all (ancient, predates RubyGems' own floor metadata) and is tracked compatibility:[] reference-only. Major 1's own gemspec declares an unrestricted '>=0' floor across its entire run (2010-2017) -- given the full tracked Ruby range rather than guessing a floor. Majors 2-4 each have a real, RubyGems-verified floor bump (2.3.0 -> 2.6.0 -> 2.7.0), confirmed exactly matching this registry's own pre-research dates (1.0=2010-03-23, 2.0.0=2017-05-07, 3.0.0=2022-09-26, 4.0.0=2024-01-19).

frameworks.name: Grape
frameworks.notes: Every date/floor confirmed live via RubyGems.org (86 published entries). Major 0's own gemspec declares an unrestricted '>=0' floor across its whole run (2010-11-13 first stable 0.1.0, through 2017), but this registry resolves each bucket to its LATEST patch (0.19.2), which depends on 'mustermann-grape ~> 1.0.0' -- and EVERY published mustermann-grape/mustermann 1.0.x release (confirmed live via RubyGems, all the way back to 1.0.0/2017-03-04) declares 'ruby_version >= 2.2.0'. So bucket 0's real, resolved FLOOR is 2.2, not grape's own unrestricted gemspec floor -- confirmed via a real failing build on Ruby 2.1 ('Bundler could not find compatible versions for gem "ruby"': mustermann 1.0.3 needs >= 2.2.0). Bucket 0's real CEILING is 2.7, not 4.0: 0.19.2's own source (grape/dsl/request_response.rb calling 'Grape::ErrorFormatter.formatter_for(new_format, {})' against a '**options'-splat method signature) relies on Ruby's old implicit hash-to-kwargs conversion, which Ruby 3.0's strict keyword-argument separation rejects outright -- confirmed via a real crash (ArgumentError: wrong number of arguments (given 2, expected 1)) on Ruby 3.0 and 4.0, and a real successful request on Ruby 2.7. Rack itself also needed pinning to '~> 1.6' in the Gemfile (see make_gemfile() in lang_ruby.py) since 0.19.2's own router crashes on Rack 2.1+ otherwise. Majors 1-3 each raise the floor further for real (2.6.0 -> 2.7.0 -> 3.3) and don't share bucket 0's Ruby-3 ceiling issue (built against modern Rack/kwargs from the start), every date/version confirmed exactly matching this registry's own pre-research figures (1.0.0=2017-07-03, 2.0.0=2023-11-11, 3.0.0=2025-11-15, latest 3.x = 3.3.5 as of 2026-07-30).

frameworks.name: Hanami
frameworks.notes: Major 0 is a genuine, permanent impossibility -- excluded (compatibility: []) after an extensive real investigation, not a convenience exclusion. Its OWN gemspec pins 'bundler, ~> 1.13' (Bundler itself enforces this against whatever Bundler version actually runs the install -- confirmed via a real failing build), fixable in isolation by pinning Bundler to 1.17.3. But hanami-0.9.2/hanami.rb unconditionally requires hanami-validations (0.7.1, its own final 0.x patch), which pulls dry-validation 0.13.3 -> dry-types (~>0.14.0, resolves to 0.14.1) -> dry-container, and this specific chain is internally version-incompatible no matter which real, published version of each dry-rb gem is chosen: dry-validation 0.13.3's own deprecations.rb calls the OLD 2-arg Dry::Configurable.setting(name, value) form (confirmed broken against dry-configurable >=0.8, confirmed WORKING against the era-correct 0.1.7); pinning dry-configurable back that far then breaks a DIFFERENT link -- dry-types 0.14.1's Dry::Types::Container (a thin wrapper over Dry::Container::Mixin) calls `config.resolver.key?(_container, key)`, a 2-arg call that fails against every dry-container release ever published (confirmed live: dry-container's own key?(key) has been a 1-arg method across its ENTIRE version history, 0.3.4 through 0.11.0), meaning dry-types 0.14.1 requires a resolver shape dry-container itself never actually shipped. No combination of real, published dry-rb gem versions satisfies both links at once. Confirmed via RubyGems (72 published entries) + hanamirb.org: Hanami 1->2 (2022-11-22) is a genuine full-stack rewrite -- Hanami 1.x's classic Rack-app-object model (a single Hanami::Application/Hanami::Action subclassed monolith) was fully replaced by Hanami 2's slice-based, dry-rb-stack architecture, confirmed via the gem's own runtime dependency list (2.x pulls in the whole dry-configurable/dry-core/dry-inflector/dry-logger/dry-monitor/dry-system family plus hanami-cli and zeitwerk-based autoloading; 1.x does not) -- not a compatible upgrade path, apps must be rewritten rather than bumped. Hanami 1's own declared floor is '>=2.3.0, <3' -- a real, explicit UPPER bound confirmed live via RubyGems, not assumed: Hanami 1 does not run on Ruby 3.x at all. Hanami 3 (2026-07-01) is very new (latest patch 3.0.1, 2026-07-03), floor '>=3.3'. Every date confirmed exactly matching this registry's own pre-research figures (1.0.0=2017-04-06, 2.0.0=2022-11-22, 3.0.0=2026-07-01).

frameworks.name: Roda
frameworks.notes: Tracked as a SINGLE bucket ('3'), mirroring this project's established precedent for other single-long-lived-major libraries (e.g. Rust's Iron) -- Roda has stayed on major 3 continuously since 3.0.0 (2017-09-15) via serial minor bumps (currently 3.106.0, 2026-07-13, confirmed live via RubyGems -- exactly matching this registry's own pre-research figure) rather than ever bumping a semver major again. Roda's real 0.x/1.x/2.x history (2014-2017, 145 total published entries across all four majors) was genuine early pre-stabilization churn before the project settled permanently on major 3 -- not tracked as separate buckets here per this registry's scope decision, the same way Padrino's own single-major history below needs only one bucket. A thin routing-tree toolkit (a single 'rack' runtime dependency, confirmed via RubyGems) -- the direct Ruby analog of PHP's Slim or Go's Chi/httprouter in this project's other registries. Declared floor '>=1.9.2' the whole major-3 line, satisfied by every tracked Ruby minor including the 1.9 bucket (1.9.3).

frameworks.name: Padrino
frameworks.notes: Tracked as a SINGLE bucket ('0'), for the same single-long-lived-major reasoning as Roda above -- Padrino has never left major 0.x since its first release (0.1.0, 2009-11-17, confirmed live via RubyGems -- exactly matching this registry's own pre-research date) through its current latest (0.16.1, 2026-03-27, also exact match; 126 total published entries). A full-stack meta-gem built directly on top of Sinatra -- its own RubyGems description literally calls itself 'The Godfather of Sinatra provides a full-stack agnostic framework on top of Sinatra', confirmed live. Its OWN top-level runtime dependencies (confirmed live) are seven padrino-* sub-gems all hard-pinned to the exact same version as itself (padrino-core, padrino-admin, padrino-cache, padrino-gen, padrino-helpers, padrino-mailer, padrino-support) -- Sinatra itself is pulled in transitively via padrino-core, not listed directly. Latest patch's declared floor is '>=2.7.8' -- a PATCH-level floor tighter than this registry's minor-level granularity (this bucket's compatibility list uses the whole '2.7' minor), the same kind of patch-vs-minor floor mismatch already flagged in this project's PHP registry for Symfony 8 (officially '>=8.4.0' but really '>=8.4.1' on the latest patch).

cryptography_libs.name: openssl
cryptography_libs.notes: Ruby's openssl gem -- unlike PHP's ext-openssl (a core, always-compiled Docker-image extension), this is a real, independently Bundler-installable gem (ruby/openssl on GitHub, RubyGems-published) that ALSO ships as a Ruby 'default gem' bundled with the interpreter itself; this registry tracks explicit Gemfile-pinned versions the same way it tracks every other library, not the interpreter's own bundled copy. Every date/floor confirmed live via RubyGems' versions API (55 published entries). Split into 6 buckets rather than just the 3 real majors (2/3/4) because the required_ruby_version floor genuinely changes WITHIN major 3 partway through its own line -- 3.0.x/3.1.x declare '>=2.6.0', 3.2.x/3.3.x raise it to '>=2.7.0' -- confirmed directly from each minor's own latest-patch gemspec, not assumed uniform across the major the way major 2 genuinely is (every 2.x minor declares the identical '>=2.3.0' the whole time, so major 2 stays a single bucket). Two real, confirmed API breaks: 3.0.0 (2021-12-24) disallows the old no-argument '{DH,DSA,EC,RSA}.new' constructor forms that 2.x allowed; 4.0.0 (2025-12-15) drops ENGINE support and SSLv3 entirely. No PQC support in any version -- confirmed no ML-KEM/ML-DSA/Kyber/Dilithium references in the gem's own source or release notes. Bucket 2's real CEILING is Ruby 3.0, not 4.0: this bucket resolves to its final patch (2.2.3), whose own extconf.rb hard-requires 'OpenSSL >= 1.0.1, < 3.0.0' against the SYSTEM libssl -- confirmed via a real failing build ('OpenSSL >= 1.0.1, < 3.0.0 or LibreSSL >= 2.5.0 is required') on every Ruby base image linking OpenSSL 3.x (bookworm/trixie, i.e. Ruby 3.1 onward, confirmed live via 'OpenSSL::OPENSSL_VERSION'); Ruby 2.6-3.0's bullseye base still links OpenSSL 1.1.1, which 2.2.3 accepts fine.

cryptography_libs.name: rbnacl
cryptography_libs.notes: A pure-FFI binding to the real libsodium C library (RubyCrypto/rbnacl on GitHub, confirmed via its own gemspec: single runtime dependency on the 'ffi' gem, no C-extension compile step of its own) -- needs libsodium itself present as a genuine SYSTEM dependency (apt-get install libsodium-dev / libsodium23 equivalent), the same system-level requirement already tracked for this project's other libsodium bindings in other languages (e.g. Node's sodium-native). Confirmed via RubyGems all 7 real majors (1 through 7, 2013-2019, 24 published entries) -- majors 1/2 never declared a required_ruby_version at all (RubyGems shows ruby_version:null for both, an old-gemspec-era gap, not a real absence of restriction), so this registry gives them the full tracked Ruby range rather than guessing a floor. Majors 3+ progressively raise the declared floor (>=0 at 3, >=2.2.6 at 4-6, >=2.6.0 at 7, latest 7.1.2 2024-10-15 -- exactly matching this registry's own pre-research figures). Classical-only (X25519/Ed25519/XSalsa20-Poly1305/Argon2, libsodium's own primitive set) -- no PQC support at any version, matching libsodium's own upstream scope. Major 1 (resolves to 1.1.0) is a genuine, permanent impossibility -- confirmed via a real crash (FFI::NotFoundError: Function 'crypto_hash_sha256_ref' not found in [libsodium.so]): 1.1.0's own lib/rbnacl/nacl.rb calls wrap_nacl_function with old NaCl-reference-implementation symbol names (the '_ref' suffix), which no packaged Debian libsodium ever exposed -- confirmed via 'nm -D' on both the oldest (jessie's libsodium13, 1.0.0) and a modern (libsodium23) build, neither has this symbol. rbnacl was restructured away from this raw wrap_nacl_function/'_ref' approach by 2.0.0 (confirmed: no '_ref' references anywhere in its source), so majors 2+ are unaffected by THAT specific bug. Major 2's real CEILING is Ruby 2.7, not 4.0, for a DIFFERENT reason: its resolved patch (2.0.0) calls the legacy Thread.exclusive method in lib/rbnacl.rb -- confirmed via a real crash (NoMethodError: undefined method 'exclusive' for Thread:Class) and confirmed live that Thread.respond_to?(:exclusive) is true on Ruby 2.7 and false on Ruby 3.0 (removed exactly there). Major 1 left as include:false / compatibility:[] the same way this registry documents every other genuine, non-fixable impossibility. Major 6's real FLOOR is Ruby 2.3, not 2.2: its resolved patch (6.0.1) added sealed-box support (lib/rbnacl/boxes/sealed.rb, calling the real libsodium function crypto_box_seal at require time, unconditionally) -- confirmed via a real crash (FFI::NotFoundError: Function 'crypto_box_sealbytes' not found in [libsodium.so]) on Ruby 2.2 (jessie's libsodium13 is 1.0.0, which predates libsodium's own 1.0.9 sealed-box addition), and confirmed working via a real successful require on Ruby 2.3 (stretch's libsodium18 is 1.0.11, well past that addition). Majors 4/5 (resolve to 4.0.2/5.0.0) don't yet use sealed boxes -- confirmed via a real successful require on Ruby 2.2/jessie for both.

cryptography_libs.name: bcrypt
cryptography_libs.notes: A native C-extension gem (ext/mri/bcrypt_ext.c, compiled via the standard extconf.rb/mkmf toolchain at install time -- confirmed via the gem's own GitHub source, not an FFI binding like rbnacl/argon2 below) wrapping OpenBSD's original bcrypt() password-hashing algorithm. Needs a real C compiler + Ruby development headers present at build time (gcc, make, the ruby-dev/ruby-headers equivalent) unless a precompiled platform-specific gem is available for the target Ruby/OS/arch combination -- bcrypt-ruby has shipped precompiled native gems for common platforms since around 3.1.19 via rake-compiler-dock, but this project's own generated Dockerfiles should not assume one is always available and should keep the compiler toolchain installed as a fallback, the same 'prebuilt binary with a source-compile fallback' pattern already used for this project's other native-extension libraries (e.g. Node's bcrypt/sodium-native). A single flat 3.x line since 2014-02-21 (3.1.3, the first stable release under this gem name) -- every published patch, including the latest (3.1.22, 2026-03-18, confirmed live matching this registry's own pre-research figures), still declares an unrestricted '>=0' floor, so this registry gives it the full tracked Ruby range.

cryptography_libs.name: jwt
cryptography_libs.notes: Confirmed live via RubyGems (56 published version entries): majors 2 and 3 are being BOTH actively, independently published in parallel right now, a genuine dual-maintained-branch situation -- 2.10.3 (2026-05-22) is actually NEWER than 3.2.0 (2026-05-13), not an artifact of stale data, exactly matching this registry's own pre-research finding. 3.0.0 (2025-06-14) is a real, intentional new major, but the maintainers are still shipping 2.x patches concurrently rather than treating 2.x as dead -- both majors declare the identical '>=2.5' floor, so this is a genuine maintenance choice, not a Ruby-version-driven split. Majors 0/1 (2011-2016) both declared an unrestricted '>=0' floor their entire run -- full tracked Ruby range. This is the SAME 'jwt' gem the jwt-pq library below depends on (hard-pinned to '~>3.0' specifically -- jwt-pq cannot pair with the still-actively-published jwt 2.x branch).

cryptography_libs.name: argon2
cryptography_libs.notes: An FFI binding (confirmed via its own gemspec: runtime deps on 'ffi' + 'ffi-compiler', not a bare C extension) around a vendored copy of the reference Argon2 C implementation -- ffi-compiler compiles that vendored C source at gem-install time, so (like bcrypt above) a real C compiler toolchain (gcc, make) must be present in the build image; unlike bcrypt there is no precompiled-platform-gem fallback path confirmed for this one. Majors 0/1 (2015-2018) both declared an unrestricted '>=0' floor -- full tracked Ruby range. Major 2 (2019-01-06, confirmed exact date live) raised the floor to '>=2.6.0' and is still the current line (latest 2.3.3, 2026-01-10, confirmed live -- exactly matching this registry's own pre-research figures). No PQC support -- Argon2 itself is a classical (non-PQC) password-hashing KDF, included here for password-hashing breadth alongside bcrypt, not as a PQC entry. CROSS-DEPENDENCY: paired with Rails on Ruby <3.1, argon2's own 'ffi ~> 1.9' dependency resolves to a platform-specific precompiled variant (e.g. ffi-1.17.4-x86_64-linux-musl) whose own floor is Ruby >=3.0 -- confirmed via a real failing build, and confirmed no Gemfile version pin can work around it (Bundler still selects that platform variant regardless of which ffi version number is pinned). Rails' own OTHER transitive dependencies (rake, concurrent-ruby, multi_json, rack-cache, and major 3's own 'bundler ~> 1.0' gemspec constraint) are all individually fixed via lang_ruby.py's own era-appropriate version pins -- this is the one remaining genuine blocker, skipped in write_context() via _argon2_rails_needs_skip() rather than narrowing this library's own compatibility arrays (the same combo works fine with every OTHER framework on old Ruby).

cryptography_libs.name: digest
cryptography_libs.notes: Confirmed live via RubyGems (and its own GitHub repo, ruby/digest) that 'digest' really is an independently gemified DEFAULT GEM -- Ruby's Digest module (MD5/SHA1/SHA2/etc.) has shipped bundled into the interpreter itself since very early Ruby, but as a 'default gem' its RubyGems-published version can ALSO be explicitly Gemfile-pinned to get a newer release than whatever shipped with a given Ruby interpreter -- the same 'default gem' pattern this registry already documents for openssl above. Confirmed live and genuinely real, not a data-fetch gap: version numbers jump directly from 1.0.0 (2020-12-03) to 3.0.0 (2020-12-18, one day later) -- no 2.x release was EVER published (RubyGems' own versions API returns zero major-2 entries). Latest is 3.2.1 (2025-10-31), exactly matching this registry's own pre-research figures. Floors: '>=2.3.0' for the 1.x bucket, '>=2.5.0' for 3.x. Pure hashing (MD5/SHA/RMD160) -- no PQC-relevant primitives, included for completeness alongside openssl/rbnacl as the project's classical-crypto baseline.

cryptography_libs.name: roqs
cryptography_libs.notes: The Ruby-equivalent-of-Go's-liboqs-go / Node's-liboqs-node / PHP's-php-liboqs slot for this project (github.com/chrisliaw/roqs, confirmed via RubyGems' own homepage/source_code_uri fields) -- a direct FFI binding calling a PRE-BUILT liboqs shared library via direct method invocation (confirmed via its own RubyGems description: 'Ruby wrapper for liboqs via direct shared library method invocation... any upgrade to the liboqs, after compiled to a shared library, roqs can immediately utilize'), NOT a bundled/vendored liboqs of its own. Needs the same liboqs C-library build-from-source recipe already established elsewhere in this project (git clone + cmake + ninja, mirroring lang_go.py's/php-liboqs' own liboqs stage) as a real system/build dependency, with the resulting .so discoverable at runtime -- this gem's own runtime deps (teLogger, toolrack) are unrelated pure-Ruby logging/utility helpers, not the liboqs binding mechanism itself. Confirmed live via RubyGems: 5 real published versions, 0.1.0 (2023-11-24) through 0.1.4 (2025-06-24), floor '>=2.6.0' the whole time -- single major, no breaking-change history yet, exactly matching this registry's own pre-research figures. MATURITY CAVEAT, stated the same way this project flags its other young liboqs bindings (.NET's LibOQS.NET, Node's liboqs-node, PHP's php-liboqs): single-maintainer, pre-1.0, included for PQC-research breadth rather than production maturity.

cryptography_libs.name: jwt-pq
cryptography_libs.notes: github.com/marcelopazzo/jwt-pq, confirmed via RubyGems -- adds ML-DSA-44/ML-DSA-65/ML-DSA-87 post-quantum signature algorithms on top of the ruby-jwt ecosystem, with an optional hybrid EdDSA+ML-DSA signing mode (confirmed via the gem's own RubyGems description). Its own runtime dependencies (confirmed live) HARD-PIN 'jwt ~>3.0' (the dual-maintained major documented in this registry's own jwt entry above -- jwt-pq cannot pair with the still-actively-published jwt 2.x branch) plus 'ffi ~>1.15' (liboqs FFI, the same class of system dependency as roqs above) and its own 'pqc_asn1 ~>0.1.0' helper gem (ASN.1 encoding for the PQ signature material). Very young: 8 published versions, 0.1.0 (2026-04-05) through the current 0.6.1 (2026-07-13), confirmed live -- exactly matching this registry's own pre-research figures. Declared floor '>=3.2' the whole time -- single-bucket major so far ('0'), no breaking-change history yet to split on.

cryptography_libs.name: pqc_rails
cryptography_libs.notes: github.com/mabutast/pqc_rails, confirmed via RubyGems -- native FFI bindings to liboqs exposing NIST-standardized ML-KEM/ML-DSA specifically for existing Rails applications (confirmed via the gem's own description: 'zero-downtime-friendly post-quantum cryptography primitives... for existing Rails applications'). UNLIKE every other crypto library tracked in this registry, this one's own runtime dependencies (confirmed live) hard-require a HOST Rails application specifically -- 'actionpack'/'activerecord'/'railties', each constrained '>=7.1, <9' -- meaning this library can only be meaningfully exercised paired with the Rails 7 or 8 framework bucket above, not standalone or with any other framework/no-framework combination; flagged here explicitly for whoever wires this into lang_ruby.py/generate_images.py next, since this project's images/<lang>/<lang_ver>/<framework>/<fw_ver>/<lib_name>/<lib_ver> structure otherwise treats the framework and crypto-library axes as fully independent. Extremely new: a single published version, 0.1.0 (2026-07-23, confirmed live -- exactly matching this registry's own pre-research figure). Also needs liboqs itself built as a system/build dependency, the same as roqs/jwt-pq above.
